key_takeaway: EdgeX currently has a more Web2-friendly front door than the first pass captured, but the underlying private integration path is still exchange-native and heavier than the docs alone suggest.

findings: The docs still describe two login paths: standard wallet login and MPC email login.
For email users, a new blockchain address is created after email verification.
The docs explicitly say edgeX will generate an EVM address for the user.
The auth docs say private APIs are authenticated with X-edgeX-Api-Timestamp and X-edgeX-Api-Signature.
The docs frame the signing flow around exporting a private key from the UI and signing timestamp + method + path + sorted params or body.
The docs do not document X-edgeX-Api-Key or X-edgeX-Passphrase in the current authentication page.
The docs expose registerAccount (Create Sub-Account) as a private endpoint.
The request body requires l2Key, l2KeyYCoordinate, and clientAccountId.
The account schema itself exposes l2Key, l2KeyYCoordinate, and clientAccountId fields.
Order creation still requires L2-specific fields such as l2Nonce, l2Value, l2LimitFee, l2ExpireTime, and l2Signature.
The L2 signing docs say critical operations use l2Signature.
The docs say users must obtain an L2 private key from the UI.
The signature flow uses ECDSA together with Pedersen hash.

signals: HTML includes a lib-privy JavaScript bundle

interpretation: The retail login surface is now more concretely Web2-friendly than the first-pass wording suggested, because the live frontend is visibly Privy-backed rather than just abstractly email-capable.
But private integration remains heavy: the production gateway enforces API key, passphrase, signature, and timestamp before deeper request validation.
This means EdgeX should still be modeled as a Web2-friendly front door over an exchange-native credential stack, not as a lightweight raw-wallet-first API venue.

There is also a stronger doc-runtime mismatch than previously stated: the docs emphasize X-edgeX-Api-Timestamp and X-edgeX-Api-Signature, while the live gateway also expects X-edgeX-Api-Key, X-edgeX-Passphrase, and a timestamp header named X-edgeX-Timestamp.

assessment.web2_friendliness: high at the frontend, medium at the integration layer
assessment.key_friction: EdgeX layers exchange-native API credentials on top of a separate L2 signing path, and even sub-account registration sits behind the private gateway.
